title: Fake Rules and a Savage Mom
paragraphs: §The Source of Your Pollution

Some Pharisees and religious scholars, who had traveled all the way from Jerusalem, showed up and gathered around Jesus. They immediately noticed that some of Jesus’s disciples weren't following the traditional rules about washing their hands before eating. See, the Pharisees—and most Jewish people back then—would never, ever eat a meal without doing a whole ritual hand-washing. They'd scrub super hard, especially if they’d just come from the market, and don't even get me started on how much they'd scrub their jugs, pots, and pans too!
The Pharisees and those religious scholars were like, "Seriously, why do your disciples just ignore the rules? Why are they eating without washing their hands first?"
Jesus shot back, "Isaiah totally nailed it when he talked about fakes like you guys. He hit the bull's-eye!"

"These people act like they're saying all the right things, but their hearts aren't really in it. They pretend to worship me, but they don't actually mean it. They just use me as an excuse to teach whatever they feel like, ditching God's actual commands and just following whatever new trends are popular."
He kept going, "Oh, great job, you guys! You get rid of God's command just so you don't have to deal with the inconvenience of following your own religious trends!"
"Moses said, ‘Respect your father and mother,’ and also, ‘Anyone who curses their father or mother should be put to death.’"

"But you guys totally wiggle out of that! You say it's perfectly fine to tell your mom or dad, ‘Hey, what I owed you? I've already given it as a gift to God!’ (This was a way to dedicate money or property to God, making it unavailable for family support)."

"By doing that, you completely get out of your responsibility to your father or mother. You basically erase God’s actual Word and scribble in your own random ideas instead. And honestly, you do a lot of stuff like this!"
Jesus then called the crowd back together and said, "Listen up, everyone—really pay attention to this."
"It's not what you eat or swallow that makes your life messed up; it's what comes *out* of you—that's the real pollution."
When Jesus got back home after being with the crowd, his disciples were like, "Uh, we don't really get it. Can you explain it in plain language?"
Jesus responded, "Are you guys seriously being intentionally dense? Don't you see that what you eat can't actually make you dirty or bad?"

"It doesn't go into your heart, only your stomach. Then it just moves through your digestive system and eventually gets flushed out." (And with that, Jesus basically ended all arguments about what foods were okay to eat; he was saying all foods are fine).

He continued, "No, it's what comes *out* of a person that pollutes them: nasty words, messed-up desires, stealing, murder, cheating on your spouse, greed, total nastiness, tricky dealings, wild parties, mean looks, gossiping, being super arrogant, and just plain foolishness—all these ugly things are like vomit from the heart. *That's* where your real pollution comes from."
From there, Jesus headed towards the area of Tyre. He went into a house, hoping no one would find him, but he couldn't stay hidden for long.
He had barely stepped inside when a woman, whose daughter was really struggling with a demon, heard where he was. She came right away and knelt at his feet, desperately begging for help.
This woman was Greek, born in Syro-Phoenicia (a Gentile, not Jewish). She asked him to heal her daughter.
Jesus said to her, "Hold on, take your turn. The children get fed first. If there's any food left over, then the dogs get it."
She quickly replied, "Of course, Master. But don't even the dogs under the table get to eat the scraps that the children drop?"
Jesus was really impressed. "You're right! Go on home! Your daughter isn't troubled anymore. The demonic problem is gone."
She went home and found her daughter peacefully lying on the bed, totally calm, with the torment completely gone for good.
After that, Jesus left the region of Tyre, went through Sidon, then back to the Sea of Galilee, and over to the area known as the Ten Towns (Decapolis).
Some people brought a man who couldn't hear or speak and asked Jesus to lay his hand on him to heal him.

Jesus took the man away from the crowd by himself. He put his fingers in the man's ears and then spit on the man's tongue. Then Jesus looked up to heaven in prayer, let out a deep groan, and commanded, "Ephphatha!"—which means, "Open up!"
And just like that, it happened. The man's hearing was perfectly clear, and he could speak plainly—just like that, instantly.
Jesus told everyone to keep it quiet, but they just talked about it even more, completely overwhelmed with excitement.
"He's done everything so well! He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak!" they exclaimed.
